findings.topic: Four observed typed query shapes and bytewise slot resolution
findings.observation: Retained caller loads RCX object and calls vptr+08 at0x180036002, testing only EAX then comparing EAX with1 on the offline branch. Getter slots+10/+18/+20 at0x180036039/3606c/36098 return RAX pointers scanned bytewise to NUL before ordered username/persona/user-id assignments. Selected StatusFunction int32_t(void*) and GetterFunction const char*(void*) match those observed shapes without a complete foreign header/class ABI claim. query_slot validates the exact four slot offsets and uses memcpy for object/vptr words, supporting readable unaligned own buffers. Wrong/stale adopted-object identity rejects before any foreign memory read.

findings.topic: Shared reservation through SDK and actual owned string copy
findings.observation: QueryUse calls begin_object before slot resolution and retains the same B26 module/object/code active reservation through typed status/getter execution. Owned copy additionally constructs the actual NUL-scanned std::string before the guard ends, closing the getter-return to borrowed-copy gap. LastError captured immediately after native getter survives string allocation and then metadata release. Actual long-copy allocations8192/12288/16384 bytes are observed once per field through SourceBackend; snapshots show exact active adopted owner and attempted destroy/free reject before effects. Raw getter returns remain borrowed and require caller serialization after return.

findings.topic: Known query failures versus invalid layout poison
findings.observation: Under the explicit non-owning query contract, SDK exception rethrows identically and leaves known live object available for explicit cleanup. Null raw return stays null; owned copy throws the prior OutOfEvidenceInput without scanning or poisoning. A real std::bad_alloc at persona copy allocation releases only reservation, preserves native outgoing error and earlier username while failing/later fields remain original. Invalid vptr/selected-slot resolution conservatively sets poison+object_unknown and ends active without owner release. Core children191/192 protect object/table page PAGE_NOACCESS after fault and prove all later queries/destroy/free reject without further memory reads or code calls; generic failure cannot pass.

findings.topic: Owned copy forwarding reaches actual worker and proxy
findings.observation: Effects gains three default owned-copy virtuals that retain the old raw-getter/null/string behavior. Core assigns username, persona and user-id via those methods in original order. OnlineExecution and RecoveredEffects explicitly forward all three owned copies, avoiding inherited defaults that would copy after an inner raw getter reservation ended. OnlinePlatform opt-in selects typed owned copies; B26-only object path wraps lower owned-copy override inside object_call; no-object legacy mode honors lower custom owned-copy overrides. Actual backend worker and a focused constructor-only RecoveredEffects proxy both prove real long-string allocation remains guarded, with explicit normal selected destroy/free before assertions. Native proxy dependencies are not invoked.

findings.topic: Negative missing-forward control is meaningful and not PASS
findings.observation: Independent comparison verifies the negative backend copy differs only by removing the three OnlineExecution owned-copy forwards; the real backend is unchanged. Same current integration source compiles this copy and exits1 on the exact active-copy/destroy-free rejection predicate after normal source cleanup. Allocation hook records missing active state but deliberately does not destroy an unguarded object, avoiding a synthetic use-after-free as the negative signal. The hook suppresses recursion for expected rejection exception allocation and restores LastError. Negative record/log/EXE and all recorded source hashes match; this expected failure is not counted as PASS.
